summary: Akira Suganuma (1934–2016) worked in Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed doctoral studies at Toyo University (ca. 1957–1962), where he later held an assistant post (1991–1994). He was also a lecturer at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies.

Akira Takeda (1930–2021) was a Sinologist who studied at the University of Tokyo (ca. 1949–1953). He served as a professor at the University of Tokyo (ca. 1978–1991) and held posts at Tokyo Woman's Christian University and Meikai University (ca. 1991–2001).

Akira Yuyama (1932–2021) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and linguistics. He studied under Jan Willem de Jong, Arthur Llewellyn Basham, Akira Hirakawa, and Naoshiro Tsuji. His posts included the Australian National University (1965–1973) and Soka University (ca. 1996–2002).

Akitoshi Saito worked in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He held posts as professor emeritus at Taisho University and as an advisor at the Kawasaki Daishi Institute of Buddhist Studies.

Alan F. Segal (1945–2011) was a religious studies scholar who studied at Amherst College, Harvard, Brandeis, Yale, and Hebrew Union College. He served on the faculty at Columbia University from ca. 1980 to 2011.

Alan Fox specializes in philosophy, Sinology, and religious studies. He earned his PhD at Temple University (ca. 1983–1988) and became an associate professor of philosophy at the University of Delaware in 1992.

Alan Gerard Wagner is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies. He completed his PhD at Harvard University (ca. 2001–2008) under the supervision of Parimal G. Patil, also studying with Robert M. Gimello and Charles Hallisey.

Alan Sponberg worked in Buddhist studies and Sinology. After receiving his PhD from the University of British Columbia (ca. 1974–1979), he served as a professor at Princeton University (ca. 1980–1988) and taught at Stanford University (ca. 1988–1991).
Alan Watts (1915–1973) worked in religious studies, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. He was educated at St Hugh's School until ca. 1928 and at The King's School Canterbury from ca. 1928 to 1932.

Alasdair Urquhart is a philosopher who studied at the University of Edinburgh (ca. 1963–1967) and the University of Pittsburgh (ca. 1969–1973). He held a post at the University of Toronto beginning around 1973.

Alastair Gornall works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and linguistics. He earned his PhD at the University of Cambridge (ca. 2009–2013) and has held posts at SOAS University of London and the Singapore University of Technology and Design (ca. 2016).

Albert Debrunner (1884–1958) was a linguist and Indologist. His career included academic posts at the University of Zurich (ca. 1914–1917), University of Basel, University of Greifswald, University of Jena, and the University of Bern (ca. 1925–1954).

Albert Grünwedel (1856–1935) was a scholar of Indology, Tibetology, and archaeology. He studied at Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich (ca. 1876–1881) and served as director at the Ethnological Museum of Berlin from ca. 1883 to 1921.

Albert Hoefer (1812–1883) was an Indologist and linguist. He served as a professor at the University of Greifswald from ca. 1840 to 1883 and founded the journal Zeitschrift für die Wissenschaft der Sprache in 1845.

Albert Thumb (1865–1915) was a linguist and Indologist who studied at the University of Freiburg (ca. 1884–1888). He held academic posts at the University of Freiburg (ca. 1895–1909) and the University of Marburg (ca. 1909–1910).

Albert Welter works in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies. He earned his PhD at McMaster University (ca. 1980–1986) under Koichi Shinohara, later holding faculty posts at the University of Winnipeg (ca. 1995–2013) and the University of Arizona (ca. 2013).

Alberto Todeschini is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied and held a post at Ryukoku University (2010–2011), and held appointments at Kyoto University and the Italian School of East Asian Studies.

Albion Moonlight Butters works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Harvard University and earned his PhD at Columbia University (ca. 1999–2006) under Robert A. F. Thurman, also studying at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies.
Albrecht Frenz (1937–2023) was an Indologist who studied at the University of Marburg under Wilhelm Rau in 1965.

Albrecht Hanisch is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies. He earned his doctorate at the University of Marburg under Michael Hahn (until 2000), later serving with the Nepalese-German Manuscript Cataloguing Project (ca. 2002–2005) and the Nepal Research Centre.
